  • Dental chartComing

    A tooth chart could be filled from the transcript and edited by click.

    The plan is a chart with canine and feline Triadan numbering for missing, fractured and mobile teeth, periodontal stage, extraction and resorption. Each finding would link to its transcript line and appear in the note and PDF.

    docs/plans/M2.md item 7 ('Not started'); docs/design/DESIGN.md section 5 Dental chart

  • Summaries of past recordsComing

    Prior records, including scanned PDFs, could be summarised on the computer and used as context for a new note.

    The plan reads scanned pages on the computer and links every summary item to its source page. History would count as context and never as evidence.

    docs/plans/M2.md item 8 and 'Decisions for the product owner'

  • Notes straight from audio (experiment)Coming

    A future option could write notes from audio without a separate transcription step.

    An audio-capable model would run as an experiment. It stays only if it comes within 10% of Parakeet's word error rate.

    docs/spikes/S2-native-linking.md configuration C; OPENSCRIBE_CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT.md section 4.4

  • Structured research outputComing

    Problem lists, diagnoses and medications could be exported as data for registries and quality review.

    Optional structured data alongside the written note is one of the product brief's goals.

    OPENSCRIBE_CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT.md section 2.3 item 8

Client documents and export

Handouts for owners that follow the vet's corrected note, plus PDFs and copy formats for any practice system.

  • Client documents that follow the vet's note

    Discharge instructions and summaries use the vet's corrected doses and spellings, in plain language.

    Discharge instructions, client summary, estimate explanation and euthanasia aftercare open from buttons under the note, with the evidence link, Copy, Save PDF and Draft again. They are never signed and are labelled 'Draft for the client: check it before handing it over.'

    engine/os-engine/src/note.rs (Reference, reference_message); apps/desktop/src/components/DocumentSheet.tsx; docs/plans/M1.md item 9; docs/guide/documents.md

  • Estimate explanation and euthanasia aftercare

    Help owners understand costs and aftercare, with accurate, gentle wording.

    Estimate explanation copies prices exactly and never adds them up. Euthanasia aftercare covers arrangements and support in gentle words.

    packages/templates/estimate-explanation/template.yaml; packages/templates/euthanasia-aftercare/template.yaml; docs/guide/documents.md

  • Medications exact, numbers checked

    Owner handouts never paraphrase or recalculate a dose, and drug names are spelled right.

    Client documents give medications exactly as in the note and write doses in digits, after a test discharge listed 'Marapitin' and doses in words. They go through the same invented-number check, with numbers the vet entered counting as supported.

    engine/os-engine/src/faithfulness.rs test numbers_the_vet_entered_are_supported_in_client_documents; docs/eval/M2.md 'Client documents'

  • Client documents in the client's language

    A discharge can go home in French from a consult held in English.

    Each document's language, any of the 7 note languages, is chosen in its panel. A French discharge from an English consult kept the medication and every number unchanged.

    apps/desktop/src/components/DocumentSheet.tsx doc-language; docs/plans/M2.md item 6; docs/eval/M2.md 'Client documents'

  • PDFs with the clinic's letterhead

    Signed notes and client handouts print as clean PDFs ready to file or send.

    PDFs carry the clinic's letterhead, visit details, the signature or a clear draft line, every heading, addenda and page numbers, on Letter or A4. The same output comes out on every platform, and citations are left out so it reads cleanly.

    engine/os-engine/src/pdf.rs (note_pdf, PageSize; tests every_builtin_template_renders_a_pdf_with_its_headings, long_notes_flow_onto_more_pages); docs/plans/M1.md item 12

  • Copy into any practice system

    Paste the whole note, or one heading, cleanly into whatever practice software the clinic uses.

    Copy as plain text (most practice systems), formatted text or Markdown, with an optional header, addenda and transcript line numbers. Each section has its own Copy button.

    apps/desktop/src/copyFormats.ts; apps/desktop/src/copyFormats.test.ts; docs/guide/documents.md; docs/plans/M1.md item 12

  • Practice system integrationComing

    Notes could go straight into ezyVet, Instinct, Shepherd, Digitail and others.

    Planned: a browser extension for web-based practice systems, an ezyVet connector, clipboard presets for desktop systems, and HL7v2 and FHIR R4 exports.

    OPENSCRIBE_CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT.md sections 4.6 and 6 (M3)

Team

Several people can share one computer, each in their role, with a record of who did what on every note.

  • Team members, roles and PINs

    Vets, technicians and reception each do what their role allows, and only veterinarians can sign.

    Veterinarians can do everything, technicians record, draft and edit, and reception records and enters patient details; the engine enforces these roles. PINs of 4 to 8 digits are stored as salted hashes with 100,000 rounds, and the first member must be a veterinarian.

    engine/os-engine/src/users.rs (Role, ROUNDS; test team_members_roles_and_pins); apps/desktop/src/components/TeamSettings.tsx; docs/plans/M1.md item 11

  • Quick switch between staff

    Staff pick their name and enter their PIN to take over the computer.

    A 'Who's using OpenBark?' picker with Switch sits at the bottom of the sidebar. The last veterinarian can't be removed while others remain.

    apps/desktop/src/components/UserPicker.tsx; engine/os-engine/src/users.rs

  • Change your own PIN

    Staff can change their PIN themselves without asking a veterinarian.

    Settings has 'Change my PIN'. A veterinarian resets someone else's PIN by removing and re-adding them.

    apps/desktop/src/components/TeamSettings.tsx ('Change my PIN'); engine/os-app/src/lib.rs set_user_pin; docs/guide/team-and-security.md

  • Who did what, on every draft

    The record shows who recorded, drafted, edited, asked for changes and signed each note.

    Each visit stores who recorded it, and each draft who drafted, edited or asked for it. Each signature and addendum records who made it, with their role.

    docs/plans/M1.md item 11; apps/desktop/src/engine.ts setActor; docs/guide/team-and-security.md

  • Roles stated plainly in the guide

    Clinics know what team roles protect against and what they don't.

    The user guide says roles keep an honest record on a shared computer and aren't a security boundary against someone with access to the computer's account. Clinic-wide accounts and audit come with the Clinic Hub.

    docs/guide/team-and-security.md; docs/plans/M1.md item 11

  • Solo mode

    Working alone needs no team setup.

    With no team set up, the app runs for one person. Your name in Settings is saved with each note you sign.

    docs/guide/team-and-security.md; docs/guide/getting-started.md

  • Clinic HubComing

    One clinic computer could serve phones and thin laptops across the clinic network.

    Planned: discovery on the clinic network, pairing by QR code, encrypted connections, a shared clinic store, an audit log and an admin dashboard. It would stay off unless Hub mode is switched on.

    OPENSCRIBE_CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT.md sections 4.7 and 6 (M4); docs/network.md 'Planned' M4

Languages

Consults in 25 languages, notes in 7, the interface in 5, with the limits stated plainly.

  • Consults in 25 European languages

    Consults can be held in English or 24 other European languages with no setting.

    Parakeet TDT v3 recognises the language automatically. Nothing needs to be chosen before recording.

    docs/languages.md; docs/plans/M1.md 'Extra'

  • Notes in seven languages

    Write the record in the clinic's language whatever language the consult was in.

    Notes can be written in English, French, Spanish, German, Portuguese, Italian or Dutch, with drug names, doses, units and numbers kept exactly as said. When the note's language differs from the consult's, the word-level check is switched off and the number check still runs.

    engine/os-engine/src/note.rs (NOTE_LANGUAGES; test note_language_is_asked_for_except_english); engine/os-engine/src/faithfulness.rs check_opts; docs/languages.md

  • App in five languages

    Staff can use the interface in English, French, Spanish, German or Portuguese.

    Each of the four translations holds 745 strings, and the app starts in the browser's language when available, falling back to English. The translations were machine-generated and are waiting for review by native-speaking veterinary staff.

    packages/i18n/i18n-{de,es,fr,pt}.json (745 keys each); apps/desktop/src/i18n.ts UI_LANGUAGES; scripts/i18n-keys.py; docs/languages.md

  • PDF labels in five languages

    The fixed words on a PDF, such as Patient, Signed by and Page 1 of 2, match the clinic's language.

    Labels come in English, French, Spanish, German and Portuguese. Anything missing falls back to English.

    engine/os-engine/src/pdf.rs (LABELS; test labels_follow_the_language)

  • Translation integrity tests

    Translated screens never lose names, dates or values from their text.

    Tests check that every translation keeps the English placeholders and that English fallback works. The build scripts check placeholders too.

    apps/desktop/src/i18n.test.ts; scripts/i18n-keys.py

  • Built-in headings stay in English

    A clinic writing notes in another language knows to rename its headings.

    Headings come from the template, so built-in headings stay in English whatever the note language. A French clinic can duplicate a template and rename its headings.

    docs/languages.md 'Note language'; docs/eval/M2.md 'Client documents'; docs/plans/M2.md item 6

  • Language limits stated plainly

    You know where checking is weaker outside English.

    Spoken-number reading and vocabulary hints work in English only. Numbers said in words in other languages may be flagged even when right.

    docs/languages.md

Models and hardware

Open models picked, pinned and tuned for the computer the clinic already owns, with optional graphics-card speed-ups.

  • First-run 'Download everything'

    A new install gets to a working note with one button, and after that it works offline.

    About 6 GB (voice detection, Parakeet, the speaker models and Gemma 4 E4B) downloads smallest first, with one progress bar, the computer kept awake and a resumable Try again. The second recogniser for number checks is a separate download on the Models screen.

    apps/desktop/src/components/SetupPanel.tsx; SetupPanel.test.tsx 'downloads every missing model, smallest first, then reports ready'; engine/os-engine/src/models.rs required_status; docs/plans/M1.md item 8

  • Model manager with a fit check

    See which models suit this computer before downloading.

    Each model shows its use, size, licence and Fits, Tight or Won't fit, estimating its size plus about 25% against 90% of graphics memory, or against 70% of (RAM minus 4 GB) without a graphics card. Fits means at most 80% of that budget and Tight at most 105%, and models that won't fit can't be downloaded.

    engine/os-models/src/hub.rs fit (test fit_uses_gpu_memory_first); apps/desktop/src/screens/Models.tsx; docs/guide/getting-started.md

  • Model names explained in plain words

    Vets who don't follow AI can understand names like 'gemma-4-12b-it-Q4_K_M'.

    Names become chips (12B, E4B, it, QAT, Q4_K_M, GGUF, MLX and others) with one-line meanings, a 9-term legend and a recommended size for this computer's memory. As a rule of thumb, E2B suits older laptops, E4B most computers and 12B cards with 10 GB or more, or Macs with 24 GB or more.

    apps/desktop/src/modelGuide.ts; apps/desktop/src/components/ModelGuide.tsx; apps/desktop/src/modelGuide.test.ts; docs/guide/getting-started.md

  • Browse Hugging Face from inside the app

    Find and add other note-writing models, with licences checked before download.

    Search lists GGUF models, most downloaded first, pinned to their current version. Permissive licences such as Apache-2.0 or MIT download in one click, and restrictive or unstated ones must be accepted first.

    engine/os-models/src/hub.rs (PERMISSIVE; tests restricted_licence_needs_acceptance, licences_are_classified); apps/desktop/src/screens/Models.tsx HubBrowser; docs/network.md R4

  • Restrictive licences only by choice

    Restrictively licensed models are never slipped in; the clinic chooses them knowingly.

    A model with a restrictive or unstated licence found in the Hugging Face browser, such as one under Google's HAI-DEF terms, must be accepted before download and is kept out of the built-in list. A test checks the built-in list has only redistributable licences, with attribution in the licence notice file.

    engine/os-models/src/hub.rs test licences_are_classified; engine/os-models/src/catalog.rs (line 160 and test only_redistributable_licenses_in_builtin_catalog); NOTICE

  • Pinned, verified, resumable model downloads

    Every model is exactly the file that was tested, and multi-gigabyte downloads survive a dropped connection.

    10 built-in models are each pinned to a Hugging Face revision with licence and attribution, and OpenBark's own downloader resumes and checks size, SHA-256 and free disk space. It was written because hf-hub 1.0 dropped resumable downloads.

    engine/os-models/catalog.json (10 models); engine/os-models/src/download.rs; engine/os-models/src/store.rs test sha256_of_known_content; docs/plans/M0.md change 4

  • Choose the note model, or bring your own

    Pick a faster or more careful model to suit the computer.

    An 'In use' panel picks the note model (Gemma 4 E4B by default) and shows the transcription and speaker models. Any .gguf model file can be used as well as the built-in ones.

    apps/desktop/src/screens/Models.tsx; engine/os-engine/src/models.rs; engine/os-cli/src/main.rs --llm

  • 'MLX optimized' labels on the MacBeing tested

    Mac users can see which models are MLX builds and aren't misled into downloading files the app can't run yet.

    On a Mac, the Hugging Face browser also lists MLX builds with a chip and a filter and points to the GGUF build that runs on the Mac's graphics chip today. Windows and Linux never list MLX builds.

    docs/adr/0009-mlx-on-mac.md Decision 1; apps/desktop/src/screens/Models.tsx mlx-chip; docs/network.md R4

  • Graphics-chip drafting on every platform

    The graphics chip is used for faster drafting wherever there is one.

    The installers draft with Metal on Apple silicon and Vulkan on Windows and Linux, including NVIDIA cards, and fall back to the processor. CUDA is used only when the browser version is built from source on a computer with NVIDIA's toolkit.

    .github/workflows/release.yml (features: vulkan, metal); install/install.ps1 and install/install.sh (nvcc check); engine/os-llm/Cargo.toml

  • Optional speech pack for NVIDIA cards

    On a Windows PC with an NVIDIA card, an 8.5-minute import is ready in about 43 s instead of about 150 s.

    Measured on an RTX 4080, the whole 8.5-minute import took 152 s on the processor and 43 s with the pack, and the number check kept pace. The pack downloads about 1.9 GB of runtime and 5.7 GB of full-precision models, resumably and checked, and Remove takes it away again.

    docs/adr/0014-gpu-speech-recognition.md (table and Consequences); engine/os-models/src/gpu_pack.rs; apps/desktop/src/components/GpuCard.tsx; commit 3888f20

  • Graphics self-test in a separate process

    A broken graphics driver can never crash the app; it stays on the processor and says why.

    After install and at each start, a separate process loads both models on the graphics card and transcribes a second of silence, and only a clean exit turns the card on. A failure shows Try again, and it was tested with every CUDA folder removed from the system path.

    docs/adr/0014-gpu-speech-recognition.md Decision 4 and Consequences; engine/os-asr/src/lib.rs

  • Speech pack state you can trust

    The Models screen shows whether the graphics card is really in use, and Remove works in every state.

    Full precision is used only when CUDA really runs, an app update that changes the runtime is noticed, and download progress survives leaving the screen. A library of the same name that was there first is kept and put back.

    commit 3888f20 ('GPU state'); engine/os-models/src/gpu_pack.rs; apps/desktop/src/components/GpuCard.tsx

  • Each recogniser on its fastest chip

    Every speech model runs where it is quickest.

    The compact speech models stay on the processor (Parakeet took 43 s on the RTX 4080 against 28 s on 6 processor threads), and the full-precision builds use the graphics card. Whisper turbo at full precision took 166 s on the processor and 22 s on the card for 5.5 minutes of audio.

    engine/os-asr/src/lib.rs provider selection; docs/adr/0014-gpu-speech-recognition.md table

  • Choose where speech recognition runsBeing tested

    IT can force speech recognition onto the processor or the graphics card while troubleshooting.

    OPENBARK_ASR_PROVIDER (cpu, cuda or coreml) overrides the automatic choice. Core ML is accepted but hasn't been measured.

    engine/os-asr/src/lib.rs asr_provider; docs/adr/0014-gpu-speech-recognition.md Decisions 5 and 6

  • One inference engine of each kind

    A stable app, free of crashes from clashing native libraries.

    Exactly one copy of llama.cpp's engine and at most one ONNX Runtime go into each program, checked in CI on Linux and macOS. whisper-rs was ruled out after it corrupted memory with a second copy.

    scripts/ci/check-symbols.sh; docs/adr/0001-inference-libraries.md; docs/spikes/S2-native-linking.md; docs/versions.md 'Deliberately excluded'

  • Chat format read from each model

    New model families work without code changes.

    Each model's own chat template, stored in its file, is used to talk to it. There are no hard-coded turn markers.

    engine/os-llm/src/chat_template.rs

  • Hardware probe and benchmark

    A clinic can see what its computer can run and measure speed on its own hardware.

    openbark probe reports memory, graphics card and processor features, and openbark bench measures time to first word, words per second and peak memory for each step. scripts/bench.sh runs a warm-up first and saves the results per computer and date.

    engine/os-cli/src/main.rs (Probe, Bench); engine/os-cli/src/probe.rs; scripts/bench.sh

  • Speech pack for Mac and LinuxComing

    Faster transcription could come to Macs and Linux PCs too.

    Core ML on the Mac hasn't been measured, and Linux CUDA needs its own pins and a test machine.

    docs/adr/0014-gpu-speech-recognition.md Decision 6

  • MLX engine on Apple siliconComing

    Macs could run MLX models directly if they prove faster.

    This comes only after measuring llama.cpp on Metal against MLX for Gemma 4 E4B and 12B on the test consults. Until then the app says MLX models need this engine.

    docs/adr/0009-mlx-on-mac.md Decisions 2 and 3; apps/desktop/src/screens/Models.tsx

  • Model slots, profiles and your own model serverComing

    Clinics could swap each model separately or use a model server they already run.

    Planned: separate slots for transcription, notes, fast edits and speakers, profiles such as 'Laptop, balanced', and an optional OpenAI-compatible server. It would be off by default, clearly labelled and never a silent fallback.

    OPENSCRIBE_CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT.md section 4.3; docs/network.md 'Planned'

Speed and progress

Speed measured on one high-end Windows desktop so far, and named steps that tick off while you wait.

  • Note ready 13.1 s after stopping

    The vet sees a draft within seconds of the consult ending.

    On a desktop with an RTX 4080 graphics card, a 9.6-minute test consult played in real time had its transcript complete 0.0 s after stop and its E4B note saved 13.1 s after stop, against a 30 s target. The same consult from a file took 76.8 s with E4B and 115.1 s with 12B on a shared graphics card.

    docs/perf/M0.md 'Live recording' and stage tables; docs/perf/results/rtx4080-win11-20261017/

  • Import board with named steps

    While a recording is imported or finished, you see each step tick off and how long is left.

    Reading the recording, Transcribing (minutes of audio done out of the total), Checking numbers with the second recogniser and Saving tick off under one bar that only moves forward, with an 'About n minutes left' estimate. The same board appears after you stop a live recording, and in the browser version uploading and in-browser conversion show as steps too.

    apps/desktop/src/components/ProgressBoard.tsx; apps/desktop/src/components/ProcessingBar.tsx; engine/os-engine/src/live.rs Stage; apps/desktop/e2e/import-progress.mjs

  • Skipped steps explained

    If a step doesn't apply, the board says why.

    When the second recogniser isn't installed, its step is marked skipped with 'Not installed: the Models screen can add it'. Skipped steps get their own icon, separate from finished ones.

    apps/desktop/src/components/ProcessingBar.tsx (state 'skipped'); apps/desktop/src/components/ProgressBoard.tsx

  • Drafting board with each heading ticked

    While a note drafts, you see which heading is being written and every step tick off.

    The board shows Loading the note model (only for the first draft after opening OpenBark), Reading the transcript with its line count, Writing the note with each heading ticked in turn, and Checking every number against the transcript. It shows the time so far and how long the last draft of this visit took.

    apps/desktop/src/components/DraftProgress.tsx (DraftBoard); engine/os-engine/src/live.rs Stage (LoadModel, ReadTranscript, Write, Verify); engine/os-app/src/lib.rs load_llm_with_progress; apps/desktop/e2e/draft-board.mjs

  • Redrafts keep the current note visible

    When you draft again, the current note stays on screen underneath until the new one is ready.

    The board names the template being used and says the current draft stays until the new one is ready, with earlier drafts kept. For a multi-pet visit it names the animal being drafted, such as Animal 1 of 2.

    apps/desktop/src/screens/Review.tsx (noteBoard, note-under-redraft, petRound)

  • Progress for heading redrafts and client documents

    Asking for a change to one heading, or drafting a client handout, shows its own progress board.

    A compact board sits inside the Ask panel while one heading is redrafted, and the client document panel shows a board with each heading of the handout. Step changes are announced to screen readers.

    apps/desktop/src/components/RefinePanel.tsx (board); apps/desktop/src/components/DocumentSheet.tsx (board); apps/desktop/src/components/ProgressBoard.tsx

  • Faster structured drafting

    The note structure is checked one word at a time, and fully only when a word breaks it. Checking every word in full was about 6 times slower with no gain in quality.

    The note structure is checked one word at a time and fully only when a word breaks it, which took E4B from 20.7 to between 45 and 58 tokens a second. Full checking was about 6 times slower with no gain in quality.

    engine/os-llm/src/llama.rs; docs/perf/M0.md fixes table; docs/eval/M1.md finding 1

  • Processor threads tuned by measurement

    Transcription on an ordinary processor runs at its fastest instead of slowing itself down.

    On 8.5 minutes of audio, 2 threads took 56 s, 4 took 34 s, 6 took 28 s, 8 took 39 s and 16 took 92 s. The main recogniser now uses a third of the processor (2 to 6 threads) and the second up to 8.

    engine/os-asr/src/lib.rs (asr_threads, second_threads); docs/adr/0014-gpu-speech-recognition.md Context and Decision 1

  • Published speed measurements

    Real timings from one high-end desktop with an RTX 4080, published with their caveats.

    On an RTX 4080, E4B read a 2,590-token prompt in 0.64 s and wrote 58 tokens a second with 3.4 GB peak memory, and 12B wrote 22 tokens a second with 7.2 GB. The graphics card was shared with a game, so these are treated as upper bounds.

    docs/perf/M0.md; docs/perf/results/rtx4080-win11-20261017/

  • 60-second drafting target on a MacBeing tested

    A concrete speed target to confirm on Apple silicon.

    The target is a 10-minute consult drafted in 60 s or less, benchmarked on E4B and 12B. The Apple silicon run is still to do.

    docs/runbooks/macos.md step 3; docs/perf/M0.md 'Pending'

  • Clean benchmarks still to runComing

    Remaining measurements are tracked in the open.

    A rerun on an idle graphics card, the Apple silicon benchmark, and the macOS disk image and uninstaller check are listed as pending.

    docs/perf/M0.md 'Pending'; docs/runbooks/macos.md steps 3 and 5

Installers and platforms

A desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux and a browser version for the same computer, installed with a double-click and removed without risk to the clinic's records.

  • Desktop app plus browser version

    Use the installed app, or the same screens in a browser on the same computer.

    A desktop app built and tested on Windows, with macOS and Linux versions built but not yet tried on real machines. openbark serve runs the browser version locally with the same screens. After a folder change or speech pack install, the browser version offers Restart now and the desktop app restarts itself.

    docs/adr/0004-monorepo-and-tooling.md; apps/desktop/src/engine.ts; docs/network.md R3; docs/adr/0013 Decision 7; docs/adr/0014 Decision 3

  • Windows setup wizard, no administrator needed

    Installs like any Windows app, without IT rights.

    A per-user wizard in English, French, Spanish, German or Portuguese installs the program apart from the clinic's data. Uninstall is in the Start menu, and a newer setup updates in place.

    docs/adr/0012-point-and-click-installers.md Decision 1; apps/desktop/src-tauri/windows/installer.nsi; install/README.md

  • Windows installer tested on a PC

    Install, update and uninstall work cleanly, and uninstalling left 13.9 GB of data untouched.

    A silent install, an update in place and a silent uninstall were run, and the 13.9 GB data folder was byte-for-byte unchanged afterwards. The delete-data path waits for a separate test machine, since the development PC holds real data.

    docs/adr/0012-point-and-click-installers.md Consequences

  • Uninstall keeps data unless you confirm twice

    Uninstalling or updating can't wipe the clinic's visits by mistake.

    The 'Delete the application data' box is unticked by default and needs a second Yes or No that defaults to No. Silent and update uninstalls never delete data, and the script uninstaller asks you to type a confirmation word first.

    docs/adr/0012-point-and-click-installers.md Decision 2; install/README.md

  • Uninstall removes the speech pack; updates keep itBeing tested

    The large NVIDIA libraries don't linger after OpenBark is removed, and updating doesn't download them again.

    After the app has closed, the Windows uninstaller deletes exactly the files listed in the pack's manifest. An update leaves them in place.

    apps/desktop/src-tauri/windows/hooks.nsh; docs/adr/0014-gpu-speech-recognition.md Consequences; commit 3888f20

  • Mac disk image with an uninstallerBeing tested

    Mac users get a drag-to-install image and a clear way to remove data if they choose.

    The image holds OpenBark, an Applications shortcut and an Uninstall OpenBark app that offers Keep my data (the default) or Delete my data with a second confirmation. The uninstaller's paths were tested with stand-in dialogs, and the real image is waiting for a test on a Mac.

    scripts/macos-dmg.sh; install/macos/Uninstall OpenBark.app; docs/adr/0012 Decision 3; docs/runbooks/macos.md step 5

  • Linux .deb, .rpm and AppImageBeing tested

    Install from the Software app on Ubuntu, Debian, Mint, Fedora or openSUSE, or run the AppImage.

    Packages appear in the app menu, and removing them keeps data in ~/.local/share/OpenBark. They are built by the release workflow and are waiting for a hands-on test.

    docs/adr/0012-point-and-click-installers.md Decision 4 and Consequences; .github/workflows/release.yml; install/README.md

  • Release workflow builds every installer

    All five installers (Windows setup, macOS disk image with its uninstaller, Linux .deb, .rpm and AppImage) come from one tagged build, and signing can be added once certificates exist.

    A version tag builds the Windows setup, the macOS disk image with its uninstaller, and the Linux .deb, .rpm and AppImage. The build fails if any installer is missing, and it can sign once certificates exist.

    .github/workflows/release.yml; scripts/macos-dmg.sh

  • Install scripts for the browser version

    Run OpenBark in a browser where the desktop app can't run.

    Double-click Install and Uninstall scripts build the browser version from source, choose the graphics option automatically and share the desktop app's data folder. CI checks that the .sh and .command scripts parse.

    install/install.ps1; install/install.sh; install/README.md; .github/workflows/ci.yml 'Install scripts parse' (bash -n on install/*.sh and install/*.command)

  • WebView2 fetched only if missing

    The Windows installer downloads nothing on a typical PC.

    Microsoft's WebView2 is downloaded only on a computer without it. The macOS image and Linux packages make no network calls.

    docs/network.md; docs/adr/0012-point-and-click-installers.md Decision 1

  • Signed installersComing

    Signing would remove the Windows and macOS security warnings on first open.

    Code signing and Apple notarisation wait on buying certificates. Until then the Mac app shows Open Anyway, and the release workflow can sign once certificates exist.

    docs/adr/0012-point-and-click-installers.md Decisions 3 and 6

    A test of background recording and on-phone models is designed with pass and fail criteria. No phone app has been built or tested yet.

    docs/spikes/S1-mobile-audio-and-inference.md; OPENSCRIBE_CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT.md section 6 (M4)

    A browser-only version could run Gemma 4 with WebGPU.

    A browser test and an installable web app are scheduled for a later milestone (M5).

Storage

The clinic decides where visits and models live, sees what will happen first, and moves data without risk.

  • Choose where models and visits are kept

    Put models on a big drive and visits on a backed-up drive or clinic share.

    Settings shows each folder with its size and free space, and Change folder uses the system picker, or a small folder browser in the browser version. You can move what's there, use a folder as it is, or start empty.

    apps/desktop/src/components/StorageSection.tsx; apps/desktop/src/components/ChangeFolderSheet.tsx; docs/adr/0013-choose-where-data-is-kept.md Decisions 1, 2 and 5

  • Folder check before any change

    The clinic sees exactly what will happen before data moves, and synced or removable drives are flagged.

    The check shows the exact folder and free space and warns about OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive or iCloud Drive folders and removable or network drives. It refuses the current folder, overlapping folders, folders inside the app's own data folder and folders OpenBark can't write to.

    engine/os-models/src/locations.rs (synced_by); docs/adr/0013 Decision 3; commit 3888f20 ('Folders inside the app's data folder can't be chosen')

  • Cloud-synced folders stay private

    A visits folder kept in OneDrive or Dropbox gives the sync service nothing it can read.

    Visits stay encrypted wherever they are kept, and the key stays on the computer. The sync service keeps copies it can't open.

    docs/adr/0013-choose-where-data-is-kept.md Decision 3 and Consequences; docs/adr/0008-encryption-at-rest.md

  • Never mixed with other files

    OpenBark's data is never spread among the clinic's other files.

    A chosen folder that already holds other things gets an 'OpenBark visits' or 'OpenBark models' folder inside it. A folder counts as OpenBark's only when everything in it is OpenBark's, so a move never sweeps up other files.

    docs/adr/0013 Decision 4; commit 3888f20 ('A folder only counts as OpenBark's when everything in it is ours')

  • Safe move with rollback

    Moving data can't lose or overwrite anything.

    On the same drive files are renamed instantly; across drives each is copied, checked and only then removed, with a progress bar, and a clash stops the move before anything changes. A failed copy is undone, and moves are refused while recording.

    engine/os-models/src/locations.rs (move_tree and tests); apps/desktop/e2e/storage.mjs; docs/adr/0013 Decision 5

  • Folder changes wait for work to finish

    Changing the data folder can't lose a draft, a signature or a patient being saved at the same moment.

    Imports, drafts, signing, edits, patient changes, downloads and recordings each hold a ticket, and a folder change is refused while any of them is writing. Late requests can't write to the old folder, and a move is put back if the new choice can't be saved.

    commit 3888f20 ('Data safety: a work gate'); engine/os-app/src/lib.rs

  • Locations IT can fix

    IT can set folder locations for managed installs.

    OPENBARK_MODELS_DIR, OPENBARK_SESSIONS_DIR and command-line options override the setting. Settings then shows 'Set by ...'.

    docs/adr/0013-choose-where-data-is-kept.md Decision 6

  • Data kept apart from the program

    Reinstalling or updating never touches the records.

    Data lives in the system's own app-data folder, apart from the program. Uninstallers never delete folders the clinic chose elsewhere.

    install/README.md 'Your data, and the recovery key'; docs/adr/0013 Consequences

  • One folder per visit, re-runnable

    Every recording, transcript and draft can be found again, replayed and redrafted, and nothing is overwritten.

    Each visit folder holds the visit's details, the audio, the transcript and numbered drafts, each with its note and template. The models and settings used are recorded too.

    engine/os-engine/src/session.rs (save_run; test session_round_trip_with_runs); docs/plans/M0.md decision 8

  • Imports kept as a playable recording

    Any imported format can be replayed and redrafted later, even if the original file is gone.

    Every visit folder keeps the audio as an encrypted 16 kHz WAV, whatever format was imported.

    commit 86d8e1b ('session folders always keep a 16 kHz WAV for playback'); engine/os-engine/src/vault.rs

  • Recordings are kept

    Audio stays with the visit after signing, so a note can be checked or redrafted later.

    The brief's default of deleting audio at signing was changed so recordings are kept with their visit. They are removed only when their folder is deleted by hand or the app is uninstalled with its data.

    docs/plans/M0.md decision 8 ('Retention changes from the master prompt'); engine/os-app/src/lib.rs (no delete-visit function)

  • Delete a visit, and a retention policyComing

    Clinics will be able to delete a visit from the app and set how long recordings are kept.

    There is no delete button for a visit yet, in the app, the browser version or the command line. An optional auto-delete policy was planned in M0 and hasn't been built.

    docs/plans/M0.md decision 8; engine/os-app/src/lib.rs; apps/desktop/src/engine.ts

  • Show files

    Open a visit's folder on disk straight from Review.

    Show files opens the visit folder in the system file manager. It is available in the desktop app.

    apps/desktop/src/screens/Review.tsx; apps/desktop/src/engine.ts canReveal/reveal

Design and accessibility

A calm, native-feeling interface that works by keyboard, screen reader and touch, in light or dark.

  • Apple-style design

    The app feels native and calm on every platform.

    The system's own font, gentle spring motion, translucent materials for floating controls only, and grouped panels with rounded corners. Buttons give a small press response.

    docs/adr/0010-apple-style-refresh.md; packages/ui/src/spring.ts; packages/ui/src/tokens.css; docs/design/DESIGN.md

  • Follows reduced motion, transparency and contrast settings

    The app respects the operating system's accessibility settings.

    Reduced motion swaps springs for short fades and stops the breathing ring, and reduced transparency makes frosted surfaces solid. Increased contrast strengthens borders and text.

    packages/ui/src/tokens.css (prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-reduced-transparency, prefers-contrast); packages/ui/src/record.css; docs/adr/0010-apple-style-refresh.md

  • Keyboard and screen reader support

    Recording, drafting and signing can be done without a mouse and are announced to screen readers.

    WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, keyboard paths, visible focus rings, status shown as text as well as colour, and labelled icon buttons. Recording started, draft ready and note signed are announced aloud.

    apps/desktop/src/App.tsx aria-live region; apps/desktop/src/components/NoteView.tsx; docs/design/STATUS.md 'Done' section 9

  • Progress announced to screen readers

    Screen reader users hear what OpenBark is doing during long imports and drafts.

    Each progress board names its bar and reads out the current step and its detail. Step changes are announced as they happen.

    apps/desktop/src/components/ProgressBoard.tsx (aria-valuetext, announced step changes)

  • Touch-friendly targets

    Buttons are easy to hit on tablets and touch screens.

    Buttons, inputs and icon buttons are 44px on touch screens, and the Record button grows to 72px. Heading tools are always visible on touch.

    packages/ui/src/tokens.css; apps/desktop/src/app.css (pointer: coarse)

  • Light, dark or system theme

    Comfortable in a bright clinic or a dim imaging room.

    A System, Light or Dark switch in Settings follows the system by default. An explicit choice is remembered on the device.

    packages/ui/src/ThemeToggle.tsx; packages/ui/src/theme.ts; packages/ui/src/ThemeToggle.test.tsx

  • Layouts for every window size

    The layout fits a large monitor, a laptop or a narrow window.

    The sidebar becomes an icon rail below 1200px and a bottom tab bar below 640px, ready for the phone apps to come. The browser version runs on the same computer only, so phones can't open it today.

    apps/desktop/src/app.css media queries; docs/network.md R3; docs/design/STATUS.md 'Done' section 4

  • Native-feeling sheets

    Side panels behave like the sheets in native apps.

    On desktop, panels float inset; in narrow windows they become bottom sheets with a grabber that follows the finger and closes on a downward flick. Dialogs scale and fade.

    packages/ui/src/Sheet.tsx; packages/ui/src/Sheet.test.tsx; docs/adr/0010-apple-style-refresh.md Sheets row

  • Works offline: fonts and icons bundled

    The interface looks right with no internet connection and calls no font servers.

    Geist fonts are bundled under OFL-1.1 as the fallback font, and Phosphor icons are bundled too. There is no emoji anywhere in the interface.

    packages/ui/src/tokens.css; packages/ui/src/fonts/OFL.txt; docs/design/STATUS.md 'Done'

  • Plain clinical wording

    Buttons and errors say what happens in plain veterinary English.

    Sentence case, buttons named for what they do, and specific error messages. 'Visit' replaced 'encounter' throughout the interface.

    docs/design/STATUS.md 'Done' section 8; docs/adr/0011-patients-and-visits.md Decision 6

  • Tested interaction details

    Buttons and panels behave predictably while work is running.

    Tests cover the record button being disabled while starting or stopping and sheets that ignore Escape while work runs. They also check that the theme follows the system and remembers an explicit choice.

    packages/ui/src/RecordButton.test.tsx; packages/ui/src/Sheet.test.tsx; packages/ui/src/ThemeToggle.test.tsx

  • Three-screen onboardingComing

    New users could be guided through setup in three screens.

    Where to run, downloading models and recording consent. It is listed as not built yet.

    docs/design/STATUS.md 'Not yet'; docs/design/DESIGN.md section 6 Onboarding

Developer and quality

Note quality is measured on realistic synthetic consults, every safeguard is pinned by tests on three platforms, and every decision is written down.

  • Note-quality evaluation

    Every change to prompts or models is measured against consults with known facts before it ships.

    openbark eval drafts each synthetic consult and scores expected vitals, doses and phrases, invented numbers (a hard fail), citation errors and, in multi-pet visits, values in the wrong animal's note. Transcripts are cached, so a prompt change reruns only the note.

    engine/os-cli/src/eval.rs (tests phrase_matching_is_forgiving_but_not_loose, numbers_are_extracted_plainly); docs/eval/M1.md; docs/eval/M2.md

  • Synthetic consults with known answers

    The scribe is tested on realistic consults without any real client's data.

    14 recorded consults, 36 minutes in all, come from 13 scripts listing the expected facts, from canine wellness and feline vomiting to equine, exotics, oncology, production animal and surgery. Each has a reference file with speaker, text and timing.

    packages/eval/fixtures/scripts/*.yaml (13); packages/eval/fixtures/audio/*.wav (14, 35.98 minutes) and *.ref.json

  • Test voices made on the computer

    New test consults can be voiced from a script, so coverage grows without recording real clients.

    A tool renders a script to audio plus its reference using Kokoro-82M (Apache-2.0), with a different voice for each speaker.

    tools/fixture-tts/src/main.rs

  • Example clinic notes for template tests

    'Template from an example note' is tested on notes written the way clinics chart.

    A SOAP note, feline dental charting by tooth and a cystotomy surgical report, each with its expected headings.

    packages/eval/fixtures/example-notes/ (dental, soap, surgery); docs/eval/M2.md item 5

  • Speaker-label scoring

    Speaker-label accuracy is measured against the truth.

    A script matches predicted segments to reference lines. It reports the speakers found and the share of speech given to the right speaker.

    packages/eval/score_diarization.py

  • Whole-recording speaker separation for batch runs

    Command-line batch runs split a finished recording by speaker, even with crosstalk and short interjections.

    The command-line transcribe, run, rerun, bench and eval paths use pyannote segmentation 3.0 with WeSpeaker fingerprints, numbering speakers in the order they first speak. The app's own imports use the live speaker tracker instead.

    engine/os-cli/src/main.rs; engine/os-cli/src/sessions.rs; engine/os-diar/src/lib.rs (tests); engine/os-engine/src/transcribe.rs test speakers_renumbered_by_first_appearance

  • Batch speaker separation tuned by measurement

    Two-person test consults are labelled as two people in batch runs, and labelling got faster.

    Raising the clustering threshold from 0.5 to 0.7 took the speakers found from 6 to the true 2, with 99.7% purity on the feline consult and 99.6% on the three-speaker multi-pet one. A window step of 0.25 instead of 0.1 cut labelling from 37.5 s to 14.9 s with identical purity.

    docs/perf/M0.md 'Fixes made during the spike'; packages/eval/score_diarization.py

  • Recognition and speaker labelling side by side in batch runs

    Command-line batch runs finish sooner because transcription and speaker labelling run at the same time.

    The wait is the longer of the two, not their sum: about 45 s together instead of about 84 s. The app's imports take the live path and don't use this.

    docs/perf/M0.md stage and fixes tables; engine/os-engine/src/transcribe.rs (used by os-cli only)

  • Offline end-to-end test in CI

    Every change proves the whole pipeline, from audio to a draft ready to sign, works with the network cut off.

    Linux CI runs transcription and drafting with networking disabled, first checking that huggingface.co can't be reached. It then requires a draft that passes the faithfulness check.

    .github/workflows/ci.yml 'Offline end-to-end (M0-2, M0-4, M0-6)'; scripts/ci/e2e-offline.sh

  • Three-platform CI

    Every change is built and tested on Linux, Windows and Apple-silicon Mac.

    Linux runs formatting, lint with warnings as errors, all tests, the symbol check and the offline test; Windows and macOS build and run the tests. A separate job typechecks and tests the interface.

    .github/workflows/ci.yml

  • 119 engine tests

    The safety logic is covered by automated tests, so behaviour can't drift unnoticed.

    Tests cover number reading, word-level checks, the second listen, vocabulary, encryption, templates, PDFs, team, patients, storage moves, licences, the speech pack and the browser version's protections. A snapshot fails if the generated SOAP structure changes.

    118 #[test] and 1 #[tokio::test] in engine/ and tools/ (grep -c, 2026-10-18); engine/os-engine/src/template.rs test generated_soap_schema_matches_snapshot

  • 43 interface tests

    The screens a vet relies on behave as designed after every change.

    Vitest cases in 14 files cover the note view, sheets, copy formats, prompt examples, translations, species, the model guide, consent, the heading editor, the Ask panel, setup, the transcript, the record button and the theme switch.

    apps/desktop/src/**/*.test.ts(x) and packages/ui/src/*.test.tsx (14 files, 43 it/test cases)

  • Browser-driven checks on demo data only

    The real app is exercised click by click without ever touching a clinic's records.

    Eight Playwright scripts cover screenshots (failing on console errors or sideways scrolling), patients with Reprocess, storage, import progress, the drafting board, a feature showcase, help videos and frames. Each runs against a demo server with its own data.

    apps/desktop/e2e/*.mjs (8 scripts)

  • Full command line

    Everything the app does can also be scripted or audited from a terminal.

    14 commands: probe, models, transcribe, note, bench, run, rerun, sessions, eval, record, devices, key, templates and serve.

    engine/os-cli/src/main.rs enum Command; engine/os-cli/src/{models,sessions,templates,record,probe}.rs

  • Audit, re-run and replay from the command line

    Reviewers and developers can re-check a saved note, re-transcribe a visit, or replay a recording as if it were live.

    openbark sessions check prints every faithfulness flag on a visit's latest note, and rerun --retranscribe transcribes the saved audio again. record --file --realtime plays a recording through the live pipeline at microphone pace, which is how the 13.1 s figure was measured.

    engine/os-cli/src/sessions.rs (SessionsCommand::Check, RerunArgs.retranscribe); engine/os-cli/src/record.rs (file, realtime); docs/perf/M0.md 'Live recording'

  • One app layer for desktop and browser

    The desktop app and the browser version behave the same because they share the same code.

    One layer holds everything the screens can ask for, and the 47 desktop commands and 43 browser routes are thin wrappers over it. Progress travels as events in both.

    engine/os-app/src/lib.rs; apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs (47 handlers in generate_handler!); engine/os-server/src/lib.rs (43 routes, excluding a test-only route)

  • Pinned versions and supply-chain protection

    Builds are reproducible and new packages aren't pulled in blindly.

    Native and inference libraries and very new releases are pinned to exact versions, ordinary ones use ranges, and lock files fix every resolved version; models are pinned by commit. Packages must be at least 24 hours old and their build scripts are denied unless allowed.

    docs/versions.md 'Pinning policy'; Cargo.toml; Cargo.lock (706 packages); pnpm-workspace.yaml (catalog, allowBuilds); docs/adr/0004-monorepo-and-tooling.md (pnpm 11 minimumReleaseAge)

  • Apache-2.0 licence with licence discipline

    The code is Apache-2.0 licensed, and nothing bundled restricts how clinics use it.

    The licence is shown in the Windows wizard, Parakeet's attribution is in the licence notice file, and GPL libraries such as PJSIP aren't bundled. NVIDIA's libraries are fetched with consent and never shipped.

    LICENSE; NOTICE; README.md 'License'; docs/versions.md; docs/adr/0007-phone-calls.md; docs/adr/0014-gpu-speech-recognition.md

  • Source published with the public betaComing

    Anyone will be able to read, check and build the code.

    The repository is private while OpenBark is pre-alpha. The source will be published under Apache-2.0 with the public beta.

    README.md ('Status: pre-alpha'); LICENSE

  • Every decision written down

    Anyone can see why OpenBark is built the way it is.

    12 architecture decision records cover inference libraries, tooling, sync, templates, phone calls, encryption, MLX, the design refresh, patients, installers, storage and graphics-card speech. Two test designs, milestone plans M0 to M2 and a list of deliberately excluded dependencies sit beside them.

    Data-safety and security problems were hunted down by independent reviewers before release.

    A review by 107 agents raised findings that were each checked by three sceptical agents, and the 30 confirmed by a majority were fixed and re-verified. The fixes cover folder moves, the browser version's protections, speech pack state and uninstall.

    The product can be renamed cheaply if a trademark search requires it.

    The name lives in one constant plus the desktop app's product name. A formal trademark search is planned before public launch.

    docs/adr/0004-monorepo-and-tooling.md; docs/plans/M0.md decision 1

How the work was done

  • Every significant decision is written up as an architecture decision record, with the alternatives and their consequences.
  • Every network call the app can make is listed with what it sends and how to stop it, and CI fails if any Rust part of the app other than the model downloader depends on a web-client library.
  • Dependency and model versions were checked against their registries and pinned to exact versions or commits.
  • Changes to speed or note quality are measured before and after, with zero invented numbers required every time.
  • A large change was reviewed by 107 independent agents, and each finding was checked by three sceptical agents before it counted as confirmed.
  • Browser tests and help videos run against demo servers with their own isolated data.
  • Deleting data is never tested on real clinic data; that path waits for a separate test machine.
  • Known weaknesses and pending device tests are published alongside the results.
